steps: Crumble the paneer coarsely with your fingers.
Heat the oil in a pan on medium and let the cumin sizzle.
Add the chopped onion, green chilli and ginger and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until the onion softens.
Add the chopped tomato and capsicum and cook for about 5 minutes, until the tomato turns mushy.
Stir in the turmeric, chilli powder, garam masala and salt, then the paneer, and cook for 2 minutes.
Take it off the heat and mix in the chaat masala and chopped coriander leaves.
Butter the bread, spread the paneer filling on one slice and cover with the other, buttered side out.
Toast on a tawa on medium, pressing down, or in a sandwich maker, until both sides are golden and crisp.
note: I went with the cooked paneer bhurji style filling with capsicum, the most common home version, and 50 g paneer for an adult sandwich. A spoon of green chutney inside works well if you have some left over.
